acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Nagas family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Serpentling, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Coil-Snap Initiate (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Short slim tail, plain dull scales, bare two-armed torso, blowgun or sling, and explicitly no hood.
Signature mechanic: Short Recoil: the Serpentling tightens its slim tail into one loop, fires, and snaps backward along that exact curve.
battlefieldDuty: Probe spacing with a short coil recoil and one low blowgun or sling shot from a plainly two-armed, hoodless silhouette.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 retain no hood and two arms with shell valves and narrow scale reservoirs; T3–T5 retain hood and multiple arms with hydraulic channels following existing hood ribs, arm bands, and relic tracks.

Affinity construction becomes visibly hydraulic beyond sacred-water symbolism through pearl cisterns, coherent filling beneath translucent scales, wet silk, pressure transfer between existing hands, and drainage at the outer coil valve.
counterplay: Step inside the recoil curve and strike the lifted outer seam before the hoodless Serpentling straightens. Affinity signal: A shell valve opens and a coherent fill line travels around the coil before the water rite; vent it at the outer curve or strike the drained matte seam afterward.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only blue scales or sacred-water decoration without hydraulic construction
Glow-only water treatment without reservoirs, coherent filling, and drainage
Invented early-tier hoods or extra arms to route water
Shapeless liquid anatomy erasing serpent and humanoid structure
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso rises from a long coiled serpent body; the T1–T2 forms have two arms and no hood, while hood and additional arms begin only at T3.
Emerald, jade, deep teal, gold, bronze, ivory, and jewel-toned scale patterns remain the family palette.
Scale, gold, gemstone inlay, silk sash, and temple stone remain separate readable materials rather than a seamless magical body.
Arm bands, gold scale bands, jeweled brow pieces, sacred script, and later hood crests communicate rank.
Coil direction, weapon-bearing hands, hood angle where present, and exposed scale seams preserve attack and counterplay readability.
telegraph: Plain dull scales overlap at one outer seam while the bare torso leans inside the small coil.
